name: Beninese Amiwo
description: Amiwo, a thick tomato-based cornmeal porridge often topped with grilled fish or chicken, is widely considered Benin's national dish.
steps_detailed: Simmer the tomatoes and jalapeño 10 minutes into a sauce.
Whisk the cornmeal into the tomato sauce with 1 cup water, cooking, stirring constantly, 12-15 minutes until thick.
Grill or pan-fry the chicken separately, 6-7 minutes per side, and serve on top.

name: Beninese Akassa
description: Akassa, fermented corn dough steamed into a firm, tangy paste, is a genuine Beninese staple, closely related to Ghanaian kenkey - real akassa's tang comes from real fermentation, not an added ingredient.
steps_detailed: Mix the cornmeal with water into a stiff dough and let ferment at room temperature 24 hours.
Shape into balls, wrap tightly, and steam over simmering water 40-45 minutes until firm.
steps: Mix the cornmeal with water into a stiff dough and let ferment at room temperature 24 hours.
Shape into balls, wrap tightly, and steam over simmering water 40-45 minutes until firm.

name: Beninese Wagashi
description: Wagashi, a firm, mild cheese made from cow's milk and a local plant-based enzyme, is a genuine Beninese specialty, especially from the Fulani community - real wagashi's setting agent isn't a distinct item here, so this leans on a widely available fresh cheese instead.
steps_detailed: Cube the paneer and pan-fry in the oil until lightly golden, 4-5 minutes.
Toss with the tomato paste and warm through.

name: Beninese Jollof Rice
description: Jollof rice, tomato-and-pepper rice cooked until it takes on real color and depth, is beloved across Benin as it is throughout much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion into a smooth puree.
Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the remaining onion, add the tomato paste, cook 2 minutes, then add the puree and simmer uncovered 15-18 minutes.
Stir in the rice and 1 cup water, add the chicken, cover, and simmer 20-25 minutes until tender.
